newsitem.title: GERMANY: BOE's George not surprised by pound correction. [CORRECTED 20:39 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BOE's George not surprised by pound correction. [CORRECTED 20:39 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and the first paragraph to make clear that George's comment referred to a downward correction in sterling today, not the initial overnight rise.)
Eddie George, governor of the Bank of England, said on Tuesday that he was not surprised by a correction to a dramatic four-pfennig surge in sterling against the mark in overnight dealings.
George, in Frankfurt for a meeting of the European Monetary Institute's council, also told Reuters that he saw U.K. inflation creeping higher after an initial dip.

Asked what he though about the sharp rise in sterling today, George said, "It has corrected quite considerably. That doesn't surprise me. Asked about longer-term market trends, he replied, "Never speculate about exchange markets."
BOE'S George says pound rise not surprising =2
Some economists have said that recent data could indicate longer-term inflation is being created in the economy.
Latest data, for October, showed Britain's underlying inflation at 3.3 percent. The U.K. government has a target rate of 2.5 percent or below for inflation.
Asked about the inflation prospects, George said, "There are some modest signs of inflation. In the short-term we see it moving to around 2.5 percent and then moving up a bit."
